title: Demo review — every field a finding can carry

findings.summary: Route cache read before invalidation completes returns a stale plan
findings.body: The async clone path snapshots routeCache before invalidation finishes. When two runs for the same hub overlap, the second plans against the first run's vehicle assignments.
findings.failure_scenario: Back-to-back scheduler ticks: run B starts while run A's invalidation is in flight, B assigns orders to a vehicle A already released, and the duplicate assignment is persisted.

findings.summary: Producer is never closed on the empty-payload early return
findings.body: The early return skips the finally block, so the producer created two lines above leaks on that path.
findings.failure_scenario: Accounts with empty windows hit the early return every tick; producers accumulate until the broker connection limit is reached, roughly six hours in.

findings.summary: Window boundary off-by-one silently drops orders booked at the slot end
findings.body: Comparison uses isBefore(end) where the previous logic used !isAfter(end).
findings.failure_scenario: An order booked at exactly 18:00:00.000 for a 16:00-18:00 slot is never fetched. No error, it is just missing from the run.

findings.summary: Null capacity profile for a vehicle type created after startup throws
findings.body: profiles.get(type) returns null for types added since the cache was warmed, and the following .weight() call throws.
findings.failure_scenario: Ops adds a vehicle type mid-day and the next run using it fails the whole solve instead of skipping that vehicle.

findings.summary: Identical coordinate pairs each trigger their own matrix fetch
findings.body: The memo key includes legType unnecessarily, so pickup and delivery legs at the same point both miss the cache. Latency, not correctness.

findings.summary: New INFO log serialises the whole problem, about 2MB per run
findings.body: At production volume that is gigabytes a day, and customer addresses end up in the log store.
findings.failure_scenario: 50 runs an hour at 2MB each is 2.4GB of log volume a day, carrying addresses and phone numbers into a system with different access rules.

findings.proposed_action: Delete the field and its import, then reply on the thread confirming it is gone.
findings.summary: Reviewer: dead feature-flag field left behind after the flag was removed
findings.body: This is what a card built from open PR comments looks like — reviewer, PR and a link to the thread, with the reply the agent proposes to send.

findings.summary: Test asserts an ordering the query does not guarantee
findings.body: The new test asserts the first result is the earliest slot, but the query has no ORDER BY. It passes today by accident of insertion order and will flake on a different engine.
